docs.title: Never let a closed deal go cold.
docs.text:
When a deal closes in your CRM, the right person finds out immediately — on Slack, WhatsApp, or email, whichever your team actually uses — and a simple weekly recap catches anything that slips through.

Works with your CRM

HubSpot Salesforce Zoho + Pipedrive, GoHighLevel, or yours

Tells your team, wherever they already talk

Slack WhatsApp Email

Logs it wherever you already track work

Google Sheets Notion Asana Trello 1 A deal closes in your CRM → 2 The right person is told immediately, by whatever channel they actually check → 3 A short weekly recap catches anything that slipped through

docs.title: The problem this solves
docs.text:
When a deal is marked as won, that's where the sales side's job ends and the ops side's job should start — but most of the time, nothing tells ops the deal closed. The handoff depends on someone remembering to mention it, which means:

  • Ops finds out about a new deal only when something goes wrong — a client calls asking where their onboarding is.
  • Friday-afternoon closes sit untouched until Monday, because nobody's watching for them over the weekend.

CloseLoop runs that handoff automatically: the moment a deal closes, the right person is told, and a quick weekly recap catches anything that still slipped through. There's no new app for anyone to learn — it talks to the tools your team already uses.

Curious how it actually works under the hood? See how it works · set it up · CRM field mapping.

docs.title: CRM field mapping
docs.text:
fromCrm() in handoff.js is the one place that needs adjusting per client. Below is the starting map for five common CRMs, based on each platform's standard deal/webhook fields. Verify against one real webhook payload from the client before going live — field names can vary by account configuration and API version; this table is the fast starting point, not a guarantee.

Our field HubSpot (Deals) Pipedrive GoHighLevel Zoho CRM Salesforce leadId dealId id opportunity.id id Id name associated contact firstname+lastname linked person name contact.name Contact_Name linked Contact FirstName+LastName phone contact phone person phone contact.phone contact Phone Contact Phone email contact email person email contact.email contact Email Contact Email team pipeline pipeline_id/pipeline_name opportunity.pipelineStageId n/a — use Deal_Source or a custom field Opportunity.RecordType or a custom field deal_value amount value opportunity.monetaryValue Amount Amount owner hubspot_owner_id (resolve to name) owner_id/owner_name assignedTo Owner.name OwnerId (resolve to Owner.Name) stage dealstage stage_id/stage_name opportunity.pipelineStageId (resolve to name) Stage StageName

Five is the starting set — the same pattern (map the client's webhook JSON into our eight generic fields) works for any CRM with a deal-closed webhook or Zapier/Make-style trigger, not just these five.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  CRM[CRM<br/>deal Closed Won] -->|webhook + secret| S[Read Settings]
  S --> E[Read existing task]
  E --> B{Build Follow-up task<br/>Closed Won?}
  B -->|no| X[stop]
  B -->|yes| Q[Follow-ups sheet<br/>add or update]
  Q --> C{Owner contact?}
  C -->|yes| W[WhatsApp alert]
  C -->|yes| G[Email alert]
  M[Monday 09:00] --> R[Read Follow-ups] --> RS[Read Settings] --> SUM[Build summary] --> W2[WhatsApp + email to each contact]

All the business rules live in one file, handoff.js. build.js copies it into the workflow's Code nodes, so the rules that are tested are the same ones that run.

docs.title: Follow-up due rule
docs.text:
Working days are Monday to Friday. Public holidays are ignored for now.

Deal closes Follow-up due Monday–Thursday 12:00 IST the next day Friday 12:00 IST the following Monday (weekend skipped) Saturday or Sunday 12:00 IST the following Monday

All times are India time (IST), computed explicitly. n8n's code runner keeps time in UTC even when the server is set to IST, so the code never relies on the server clock's timezone.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
A task is always written, even when something is wrong, and the problem is spelled out in the Flags column and the alert:

Flag Meaning Missing: lead id, sales owner Required fields the CRM didn't send at Closed Won Closed on a weekend → Monday slot The deal closed Saturday or Sunday No owner set for team Enterprise Nobody in Settings to alert, so the row is written without a message

docs.title: When the same deal comes in again
docs.text:
The workflow matches on the CRM's lead/deal ID.

  • It updates the row and sends an alert starting with Updated:.
  • The Status is never overwritten. A deal marked Contacted stays Contacted.
  • Waiting time counts from the first arrival, not the latest edit.

docs.title: Weekly summary
docs.text:
• Who it covers: only open tasks (New).
  • What it counts: follow-ups due in the next 7 days, overdue follow-ups, and tasks with no owner set.
  • Who's at the top: the three tasks waiting longest.

It goes to every owner listed in Settings, as the agenda for the weekly review.

docs.title: What's real and what's sample
docs.text:
• Real: the workflow, the rules, and their tests (same engine as a prior real deployment — see git history).
  • Sample:
  • Every lead is invented. send-test.sh posts a generic CRM-shaped lead.
  • The field names in fromCrm() are a starting point for five common CRMs (see the mapping), not confirmed against any specific client yet. Capture one real webhook payload before going live.
  • WhatsApp uses Meta's free test number pattern from the original deployment. In production it would go through a WhatsApp provider such as WATI (n8n-nodes-wati, Send Template Message) with an approved message template.

docs.text: File What handoff.js All rules: CRM field mapping, follow-up due date, flags, alert text, weekly summary handoff.test.js Fixed-date checks for every rule (node handoff.test.js) build.js Builds workflow.json with handoff.js inlined into the Code nodes workflow.json Import into n8n (no credentials inside) payloads/, send-test.sh Sample CRM leads and the script that sends them

docs.text:
Part State Rules (follow-up due date, flags, weekly summary) Built and tested, in Node and inside n8n Workflow in n8n Built, generic CRM webhook with a secret header Email alerts + Google Sheet end-to-end Logic tested (node handoff.test.js); not yet run against a live Sheet/Gmail for this generic version WhatsApp alerts Wired, same pattern as the original deployment; needs a WhatsApp Business account with billing to actually send A real CRM connection Sample payloads only — see the field mapping. Capture one real webhook payload per client and adjust fromCrm()

The weekly review runs every Monday at 09:00 IST. Ops/Sales closes the loop in the Sheet by changing Status: New → Contacted.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text: You need Docker and Node 18+. Node is only used for the tests and build.js; n8n itself runs in Docker.

docs.title: 1. Run n8n locally
docs.text:
From the repo folder:

docker run -d --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata -e TZ=Asia/Kolkata -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n -v "$PWD:/files" docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n

Open http://localhost:5678 and create your login.

docs.title: 2. Google Sheet
docs.text:
Create a Sheet with two tabs.

Follow-ups: row 1 headers, in this order:

Received at, CRM Lead ID, Lead, Phone, Email, Team, Deal Value, Owner, Follow-up due, Status, Flags
  • Give Status a dropdown: New, Contacted.
  • Format Received at and Follow-up due as plain text (Format → Number → Plain text). Otherwise dates that get retyped won't count in the weekly summary.

Settings: headers Role, Team, Name, WhatsApp, Email:

Role Team Name WhatsApp Email Trigger stage Closed Won Team Owner Enterprise name number email Team Owner SMB name number email Fallback Owner name number email
  • Format the WhatsApp column as plain text, and write numbers with the country code, e.g. 919800000001.
  • Fallback Owner is used when a deal's team doesn't match any Team Owner row.
  • Trigger stage is the CRM stage that creates a task — rename to match the client's actual "won" stage name.

docs.title: 3. Credentials in n8n
docs.text:
• Google Sheets OAuth2 and Gmail OAuth2 (one OAuth client covers both; enable the Sheets, Drive and Gmail APIs):
  • In Google Cloud, create an OAuth client with redirect URI http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback.
  • Add the credential in n8n and sign in.
  • WhatsApp:
  • On developers.facebook.com, create an app and add WhatsApp.
  • On API Setup, add and verify your phone as a recipient. Copy the Phone number ID, the WhatsApp Business Account ID and the access token into an n8n WhatsApp API credential.
  • Send "hi" from your phone to the test number. Plain-text messages only work within 24 hours of a message from your side.
  • Webhook secret:
  • Create a Header Auth credential named CRM webhook secret, with header name X-Handoff-Secret and a long random value.
  • Copy .env.example to .env and put the same value in it.

docs.title: 4. Build, import, publish
docs.text:
SHEET_ID=<sheet id> WA_PHONE_ID=<phone number id> node build.js

docker exec n8n n8n import:workflow --input=/files/workflow.json && docker exec n8n n8n publish:workflow --id=crmFollowupHandoff1 && docker restart n8n

Open the workflow and pick your credentials on the webhook node, every Google Sheets node and both WhatsApp nodes. Then publish. Re-importing resets the credential picks, so pick them again after every rebuild.

docs.title: 5. Try it
docs.text:
./send-test.sh payloads/closed-won.json
Payload What should happen closed-won.json New row in Follow-ups, WhatsApp to the Enterprise team's owner same file again Still one row; the alert starts Updated: missing-fields.json Row with Flags Missing: lead id, sales owner, alert starts ⚠ closed-lost.json Nothing: not Closed Won

To see the weekly summary now, open Monday 09:00 in the editor and click Execute workflow.

To run the rule tests: node handoff.test.js should print handoff ok.

docs.title: Going live with a real CRM
docs.text:
Route 1: webhook (recommended).

  1. In the client's CRM, create one webhook on the deal-closed event (see the field mapping for where that lives per CRM).
  2. Point it at the production webhook URL and add the custom header X-Handoff-Secret.
  3. Don't subscribe to more than one overlapping event. A duplicate firing at the same moment could create a duplicate row.
  4. n8n must be reachable from the internet: n8n Cloud, or a tunnel.

Route 2: polling, if the CRM has no webhook.

  1. Enable the two greyed-out nodes.
  2. Point CRM – Fetch recently updated deals at the client's actual API and auth.
  3. Map the response to the same fields before Build Follow-up task.

Production WhatsApp: swap the WhatsApp nodes for your provider's node (for WATI, n8n-nodes-wati → Send Template Message) with an approved utility template.

Before going live: capture one real webhook payload from the client's CRM and adjust fromCrm() in handoff.js to the real field names — start from the 5-CRM mapping if they use HubSpot, Pipedrive, GoHighLevel, Zoho, or Salesforce.
